LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony? how much more sugar was bought?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. adopt the use of interrogatives used in oral and written texts. Learner is guided to: • Mention the words used to ask questions - how, what, when, why, who. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications. • Use the wh- words and how to ask questions collaboratively. • Construct questions using the pattern: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony? how much more sugar was bought? • Use the interrogatives with: else, much ... to complete sentences. • Use digital devices to practice constructing questions with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could 1. Why do we ask questions? 2. How do we ask questions? 97 use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology or be assisted to operate the devices.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
